components.name: BTQ Bitcoin Quantum
components.description: First quantum-safe fork of Bitcoin. Testnet v0.3.0 (Mar 2026) is the first working implementation of BIP-360 Pay-to-Merkle-Root (P2MR) outputs: SegWit v2 outputs with bc1z (bech32m) addresses, Merkle-root commitment verification, control-block validation, and all five Dilithium (ML-DSA) post-quantum signature opcodes enabled in P2MR tapscript context. Replaces ECDSA/Taproot internal-key exposure with NIST-standardized ML-DSA signatures. Testnet V3 surpassed 200,000 blocks and 50+ miners as of Mar 2026.

Open-sourced testnet with readiness assessments and migration test environments. $20M Series A funding announced January 2026.

components.name: SEALSQ Quantum Shield QS7001

QS7001 V1 reached production-sample availability in Mar 2026; V2 (full PQC algorithm API) targets engineering samples Jul 2026 and production samples Oct 2026. Common Criteria evaluation in progress via accredited labs (e.g. SERMA Technologies); V1 Hardware Evaluation Test Report expected end of Mar 2026, V2 ETR targeted Sep 2026. QVault-TPM line also tracks toward FIPS 140-3. Protects against harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks.

components.name: Forward Edge-AI Isidore Quantum
components.description: Hardware-based plug-and-play post-quantum encryption platform. NSA CNSA 2.0 compliant protocol-agnostic solution working with legacy and modern networks. Features one-way data diode with NIST-approved PQC algorithms including ML-KEM. Tested by U.S. military branches with SpaceX deployment. Secures data in transit without software rewrites or PKI dependencies.

components.name: QuSecure QuProtect R3
components.description: First end-to-end cryptographic security platform for quantum era. Provides cryptographic discovery (Recon) crypto-agility engine (Resilience) and real-time compliance reporting. Enables dynamic cipher key and algorithm updates without code changes or downtime. Works across cloud on-premise and edge environments. Includes QuEverywhere for mobile PQC.

components.name: SandboxAQ AQtive Guard
components.description: Platform for automated discovery and inventory of cryptographic assets. Facilitates transition to post-quantum cryptography and enhances cyber readiness against AI-powered attacks. Provides continuous visibility into cryptographic dependencies. Deployed in U.S. Department of War (DoW) CIO systems (per Dec 2025 press release; DoD renamed to Department of War in 2026). HQC algorithm contributor selected by NIST.

components.name: 01 Quantum IronCAP

Not standard Classic McEliece. Powers Hitachi DoMobile Ver.5 remote access system in Japan. Developing Quantum AI Wrapper (QAW) for securing AI data with Full Homomorphic Encryption and Quantum Crypto Wrapper (QCW) for blockchain quantum-safety.

ML-KEM is now implemented (not merely planned); as of cryptography 48.0.0, ML-KEM works without liboqs.

components.name: Cisco ASA (Adaptive Security Appliance)
components.description: Per Cisco Secure Firewall PQC roadmap: ASA 9.18+ supports RFC 8784 (PSK mixing in IKEv2); ASA 9.19+ supports RFC 9242 and RFC 9370 hybrid key exchange. ML-KEM support arrives in ASA 9.25 / FTD 10.5 (targeted late 2026); ML-DSA and broader PQC planned for ASA/FTD 11.0 (2H 2027). GA release line is 9.24(x).

components.name: Cisco Meraki MX (Cloud-Managed Firewall)
components.description: Cisco Meraki MX is a cloud-managed next-generation firewall/SD-WAN platform used heavily in branch offices and SMB/enterprise deployments. AutoVPN uses IKEv2/IPsec with classical algorithms. Meraki cloud dashboard communications use TLS 1.3 (classical). New C8455-G2-MX hardware announced as AI/ML and PQC-ready. PQC follows Cisco's quantum-safe roadmap — no specific Meraki firmware PQC timeline published.

components.name: Fortinet FortiGate (FortiOS)
components.description: Fortinet FortiGate is the market-leading enterprise firewall/NGFW. FortiOS 7.6.x supports ML-KEM (Kyber), BIKE, HQC, and Frodo for IPsec key exchange per RFC 9370. FortiOS 8.0 (2026) extends PQC to management and SSL inspection. FortiGate is critical for APAC enterprise and government networks.

components.name: NGINX Plus
components.description: NGINX Plus R33+ PQC via OQS provider for OpenSSL 3.5.

components.name: Kubernetes

components.name: Istio Service Mesh
components.description: Istio adds a Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) option to COMPLIANCE_POLICY since v1.27 (Aug 2025): enforces TLS 1.3, TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256/TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, and post-quantum-safe key exchange X25519MLKEM768 for Envoy/ztunnel mTLS, downstream/upstream TLS, and the Istio xDS server. meshConfig.tlsDefaults.ecdhCurves can be set to X25519MLKEM768.

components.name: Linkerd
components.description: Linkerd 2.19 defaults to ML-KEM-768 for mTLS key exchange in service mesh.

components.name: OpenVPN
components.description: OpenVPN with OpenSSL 3.5 supports ML-KEM/ML-DSA. Hybrid ECDHE-MLKEM deployable.

components.name: Cisco Secure Client (AnyConnect)
components.description: Cisco Secure Client (formerly AnyConnect) is the most widely deployed enterprise VPN client, using SSL/TLS and IKEv2/IPsec for VPN tunnels. Cisco has published a roadmap for its Secure Firewall headend (ASA/FTD): ML-KEM and ML-DSA support for Remote Access VPN targeted for ASA/FTD 11.0 in H2 2027, pending IETF RFC standardization. This roadmap covers the ASA/FTD headend, not the Secure Client application specifically -- Cisco has not published a separate PQC timeline for the Secure Client app itself. Migration will require both client and headend upgrades.

components.name: Apache Traffic Server
components.description: Apache Traffic Server: CDN/proxy. Uses OpenSSL. PQC available with OpenSSL 3.5+.

components.name: Eclipse Jetty
components.description: Eclipse Jetty: Java web server. PQC depends on JDK. Java 24+ has ML-KEM/ML-DSA.

components.name: GitLab CI/CD
components.description: GitLab CI/CD: built partially in Go. gitlab.com servers use PQC TLS from Go 1.24+.

components.name: OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect (OIDC)
components.description: Not stated. The document describes standard cryptographic protocols (OAuth 2.0, OIDC, JWT) but contains no mention of Post-Quantum Cryptography algorithms, implementations, or migration plans.

components.description: MySQL: database. Uses OpenSSL for TLS. PQC available with OpenSSL 3.5+.

components.name: MariaDB Server
components.description: MariaDB: database. Uses OpenSSL/wolfSSL for TLS. PQC available with OpenSSL 3.5+.

components.name: Fireblocks
components.description: Fireblocks research team is mapping candidate PQC signature schemes (ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, FN-DSA plus NIST Round 2 candidates) for its MPC co-signer architecture, and auditing internal crypto infrastructure (certificates, data-at-rest, TLS) for post-quantum readiness. Approach centers on cryptographic agility, threat modeling, and standards engagement; recommends industry quantum readiness by 2030. No production PQC implementation or specific deployed algorithm yet.

components.name: DFNS
components.description: The document states the HSM Service offers "Quantum-safe cryptography support" to future-proof security infrastructure for the post-quantum era. No specific PQC algorithms or current production implementation details are provided; it is described as a capability of the IBM Crypto Express integration.

components.name: Taurus SA
components.description: Taurus co-leads an open-source post-quantum signature initiative with Project Eleven and Zooko Wilcox (Zcash). It introduced ML-DSA-B, a variant of the NIST standard ML-DSA (FIPS 204) replacing internal hashing with BLAKE3 for up to 60x faster pre-hash, ~20% faster signing, ~30% faster verification. Taurus CSO Jean-Philippe Aumasson co-authored SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) and BLAKE. Forward-looking engineering effort ('cheap insurance policy'), not yet a production custody-signing deployment.

components.name: BitGo
components.description: In May 2026 BitGo, with Silence Laboratories, completed what it describes as the first post-quantum MPC transaction simulation by a regulated custodian, using Silence Labs' PQ-MPC protocol built on ML-DSA (NIST FIPS 204) integrated with BitGo's custody platform. Described as a demonstration/simulation, with continued refinement through select partners rather than immediate production rollout.

components.name: Coinbase Custody
components.description: Coinbase plans to introduce 'quantum-proof' custody services for institutional clients by late 2026, combining existing encryption with emerging NIST-reviewed post-quantum standards (hybrid approach, no single algorithm committed yet). A Coinbase advisory board of cryptographers (convened Jan 2026) published a ~50-page position paper in April 2026 on quantum threats to blockchain; CEO Brian Armstrong also leads an industry coalition pushing Winternitz/BIP-360 for Bitcoin.

components.name: Bitcoin Core
components.description: Current Bitcoin addresses are not quantum resistant. BIP 360 proposes a "first step" via Pay-to-Merkle-Root (P2MR) to protect against long-exposure attacks by removing keypath spend. The team intends to introduce post-quantum signature schemes for short-exposure protection in future proposals.

components.name: Ethereum (Geth)
components.description: Ethereum has a published quantum-resistance roadmap (ethereum.org/roadmap/future-proofing). It targets: replacing consensus-layer BLS signatures with hash-based Winternitz signatures aggregated via STARKs; moving from KZG commitments to STARK-based data availability; enabling post-quantum user account signatures via native account abstraction (EIP-8141); and migrating ZK proofs from elliptic-curve SNARKs to STARKs. The Ethereum Foundation launched a post-quantum security hub/roadmap in March 2026 with 10+ client teams. Not yet implemented on mainnet.

components.name: Solana
components.description: On 2026-04-27 the Solana Foundation confirmed core teams (Anza and Jump's Firedancer) independently selected Falcon as the network's post-quantum signature scheme (compact signatures), with early implementations already on GitHub. A phased three-step roadmap was published: (1) continue research/evaluate Falcon, (2) adopt PQC for new wallets when quantum becomes a credible threat, (3) migrate existing wallets. Blueshift's Winternitz (WOTS) Vault has been live on mainnet >2 years and was cited by Google Quantum AI as a leading shipped quantum-resistant primitive.

components.name: QRL
components.description: QRL 2.0 / Project Zond Testnet V2 launched 2026-03-31 as an EVM-compatible PoS network. PQC: ML-DSA-87 (CRYSTALS-Dilithium) is the primary signature scheme (mandatory for staking validators, stateless/unlimited signatures); XMSS (stateful, one-time keys) retained from the original 2018 mainnet; SLH-DSA/SPHINCS+ recognized at the wallet-descriptor level; Falcon-1024 and ML-KEM being implemented to secure peer-to-peer networking. The in-house Hyperion compiler (a post-quantum superset of Solidity) lets smart contracts natively verify quantum-secure signatures. An independent Halborn cryptography audit completed 2026-04-03 with no vulnerabilities; mainnet is gated on audit completion.

components.name: Algorand
components.description: Algorand has executed the first post-quantum transaction on its mainnet using NIST-selected Falcon signatures (Falcon-1024). The protocol uses Falcon for state proofs every 256 rounds and supports PQC transactions via Logic Signatures. While production-grade code exists, general account and consensus layer integration is described as experimental.

components.name: Cardano
components.description: Input Output Research conducts advanced research in post-quantum cryptography as part of its fundamental research (SRL 1–2) and technology validation (SRL 3–5). The text states they are pioneering foundational research but does not confirm production implementation or specific algorithms currently deployed on the Cardano mainnet.

components.name: IOTA
components.description: IOTA Identity v1.7 (beta, released 2025-10-17) adds NIST-standardized post-quantum signatures: ML-DSA (security levels 44, 65, 87), SLH-DSA (128/192/256), and FALCON (512/1024), plus hybrid composite signatures id-MLDSA44-Ed25519 and id-MLDSA65-Ed25519 for Verifiable Credentials. Currently an experimental feature for developers (dependent on key-storage support). (Legacy Tangle used Winternitz OTS.)

components.name: Cosmos/Tendermint
components.description: The project aims to replace Ed25519 with the Dilithium signature algorithm in Tendermint/CometBFT and Cosmos-SDK. Preliminary tasks include a functioning Tendermint core with Dilithium, key generation, and network startup. Full integration into cosmos-app-pqc is planned to support transfers, staking, governance, and CosmWasm.

components.name: Aptos
components.description: Proposal (AIP-137, Draft status) to add SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s signatures for accounts. Implementation details include 48-byte secret keys and 32-byte public keys. Benchmarks show verification is ~5x slower than Ed25519. Future support for ML-DSA and Falcon is mentioned as potential alternatives but not currently implemented.

components.name: Avalanche
components.description: Proposal for a staged transition using a Hybrid Signature Model combining ECDSA with Falcon/Dilithium. Includes C-Chain precompiles for PQC verification and Subnet Modularity for testing PQ-only environments before mainnet enforcement. Currently in technical review phase via ACP repository.

components.name: Sui
components.description: Sui is designed for cryptographic agility but currently uses classical primitives. Transition strategies are defined, including proactive multisig and adaptive ownership transitions. NIST-recommended algorithms like ML-DSA (Dilithium), FALCON, SPHINCS+, and ML-KEM (Kyber) are identified for future adoption. Batch verification optimizations for PQ signatures are currently lacking compared to ECC.

components.name: Broadcom Avi (NSX ALB)
components.description: Application delivery controller and load balancer (formerly Avi Networks / VMware NSX ALB) with L4-L7 load balancing, WAF, and service mesh integration. Version 31.2.1 ships GA PQC: pure ML-KEM, hybrid KEMs, and ML-DSA for TLS 1.3. Note: not supported with Intel QAT or FIPS-enabled deployments.

components.name: Fortinet FortiGate-Rugged
components.description: FortiOS 7.6+ includes PQC (ML-KEM, BIKE, HQC, Frodo). Applies to all FortiGate models.

components.name: evolutionQ BasejumpQDN
components.description: Software for building a Quantum Delivery Network (QDN). Provides intelligent quantum-safe key routing across extended fiber distances beyond QKD's natural ~300 km limit using trusted repeater nodes. Vendor-neutral — works with QKD hardware from ID Quantique, Toshiba, and other vendors, preventing lock-in. Includes BasejumpSIM cloud-based simulation tool for modeling QDN deployments before physical rollout. Deployed in production with Nokia and ID Quantique for Proximus (Belgian telecom) live hybrid quantum encryption key trial over an optical network.

components.name: evolutionQ BasejumpSKI
components.description: Symmetric Key Infrastructure (SKI) combining symmetric pre-shared keys (PSK), ECDH, and post-quantum cryptography (ML-KEM) in a multimodal key establishment approach. Delivers hybrid quantum-safe end-to-end encryption keys without requiring QKD hardware or significant infrastructure changes. Designed as a drop-in complement to BasejumpQDN for organizations in early PQC migration stages or those not yet deploying QKD hardware. Implements evolutionQ MultimodalKES protocol for defense-in-depth protection against quantum and classical threats. [Note: release date predates FIPS 203/204/205 finalization (Aug 2024); may reference draft/pre-standard algorithms.]

components.name: Qrypt BLAST SDK
components.description: REST API and SDK implementing the BLAST (Bounded Leakage-Abuse Symmetric-key Transport) algorithm for generating identical symmetric encryption keys independently at multiple endpoints — without transmitting keys over the network. Eliminates the key distribution problem. Powered by quantum entropy sourced from ICFO (Spain), Los Alamos National Lab, Oak Ridge National Lab, and EPFL (Switzerland). Peer-reviewed algorithm (Prof. Yevgeniy Dodis, NYU). Available as cloud API and on-premises. AWS Marketplace listed. Partnership with Fortanix for multi-source quantum entropy compliance (March 2026). Supports GDPR and CNSA 2.0 compliance needs.

components.name: ISARA Advance
components.description: Autonomous cryptographic inventory and risk assessment tool from ISARA Corporation. Continuously catalogs and monitors cryptographic assets across environments — algorithms, protocols, devices, certificates, and keys. Provides risk-prioritized migration roadmap for transitioning to post-quantum cryptography. Designed as a companion discovery tool to ISARA Radiate (PQC algorithm library), enabling organizations to assess their cryptographic exposure before beginning PQC remediation. Supports enterprise-wide CBOM generation and compliance gap analysis.

components.name: 1Password
components.description: 1Password deployed hybrid post-quantum key exchange (X25519MLKEM768) for all 1Password web application TLS connections, announced 2026-03-31. Combines classical X25519 with ML-KEM-768; protects against harvest-now-decrypt-later. Works automatically in compatible browsers (Chrome, Firefox) with no config or performance penalty. This is phase one of a broader roadmap to expand PQC coverage across products.

components.name: Gmail / Google Workspace
components.description: Google's cloud email and productivity platform. Transport layer protected by ML-KEM hybrid TLS via BoringSSL on Google's servers — HNDL-resistant for email in transit since 2024. S/MIME end-to-end encryption uses classical RSA/ECDSA certificates with no PQC S/MIME certificate issuance available. Google Workspace Client-Side Encryption (CSE) uses classical ECDH key wrapping. Full PQC for message content depends on PKI ecosystem and S/MIME standards maturity.

components.name: WhatsApp
components.description: WhatsApp uses Signal Protocol PQXDH for post-quantum initial key establishment.

components.name: VIAVI TeraVM Security Test
components.description: Cloud-enabled platform for benchmarking enterprise VPN gateways and IPSec systems migrating to NIST PQC algorithms. Security Test module emulates tens of thousands of concurrent users with realistic application traffic while measuring PQC-specific KPIs: handshake latency, SA establishment time, re-keying overhead, key size impact. Supports hybrid scenarios (PQC initiator plus classical responder) to validate backward compatibility. Key finding: IKEv2 SA establishment increases from 38ms (classical) to 12626ms with some PQC configurations. Partnership with QNu Labs for QKD/QRNG/hybrid PQC test badging. [Note: release date predates FIPS 203/204/205 finalization (Aug 2024); may reference draft/pre-standard algorithms.]

components.name: Keysight CyPerf
components.description: Cloud-native network security test platform validating hybrid post-quantum TLS 1.3 handshakes using X25519+ML-KEM-768 across distributed physical and cloud environments. Version 7.0.2 (Oct 2025) supports hybrid key exchange simulation with Cloudflare endpoint. Stateful traffic generation at 1; 10; 100; 400 Gbps. Community Edition available free. Integrates with BreakingPoint System via ATI-2025-15 application for hybrid PQC encrypted traffic simulation in security appliance testing.

components.name: Keysight Inspector
components.description: Device security testing platform (via Riscure acquisition) using Crypto 3 modular framework for PQC side-channel and fault injection testing. Dilithium TVLA data generator and Known Key Analysis module validate ML-DSA implementations against power; timing; and electromagnetic side-channel leakage. ML-KEM and SLH-DSA support in pre-release. Captures millions of power traces per second using PXI-based DS1050A testbench. Collaborated with NXP on ML-DSA countermeasure validation and PQShield on industry readiness. Supports FIPS 140-3 Level 4 compliance verification for semiconductor and device vendors.

components.name: CryptoNext COMPASS Network Probe
components.description: Passive high-performance cryptographic data detection system deploying on network taps and SPAN ports. Identifies all cryptographic algorithms; key types; and certificate details across 100+ IT and OT protocols in real time without packet injection. First EU company to achieve NIST CAVP certification for all three finalized PQC algorithms (ML-KEM/FIPS 203; ML-DSA/FIPS 204; SLH-DSA/FIPS 205) in June 2025. On path to FIPS 140-3 module certification. Integrates with COMPASS Analytics Platform for governance reporting. Recommended by NIST NCCoE for cryptographic discovery in PQC migration workflows. Secure boot; hardened OS; integrity checks; PQC-secured TLS 1.3 management communications.

components.name: pqcscan
components.description: High-performance open-source PQC readiness scanner written in Rust. Two scan modes: tls-scan (probes HTTPS/TLS endpoints for PQC algorithm support; TLS version; cipher suite; hybrid key exchange detection) and ssh-scan (probes SSH servers for PQC host key and key exchange support). Outputs JSON with HTML report generation. Binary releases for Linux; macOS; Windows. Database filtering for detecting specific PQC algorithm OIDs. Developed by Anvil Secure. [Note: release date predates FIPS 203/204/205 finalization (Aug 2024); may reference draft/pre-standard algorithms.]

components.name: pqc-flow
components.description: Detects PQC and hybrid algorithm usage in live network traffic and PCAP captures. SSH detection: sntrup761x25519-sha512@openssh.com (OpenSSH 9.0+), mlkem, kyber, ntruprime variants via custom SSH_MSG_KEXINIT parser. TLS 1.3 detection: X25519Kyber768 (Chrome 0x11ec), X25519Kyber768Draft00 (Cloudflare 0xfe31/0x6399), NIST ML-KEM drafts (0x2001-0x2010) via custom ClientHello/ServerHello supported_groups and key_share extension parser. QUIC detection via TLS-in-QUIC handshake parsing. IKE/IPsec via nDPI classification. PQC flags bitmask tracks KEM presence, signature presence, hybrid negotiation, offered-only, and session resumption states. No nDPI patches required for SSH/TLS PQC extraction.

components.name: PQC-LEO
components.description: Open-source PQC benchmarking and evaluation framework automating computational and network performance measurement for NIST PQC algorithms. Uses OpenSSL with OQS provider to run standardized TLS 1.3 performance tests across x86 and ARM architectures. Measures: handshake latency; key generation time; signing/verification overhead; memory footprint; energy consumption. Generates comparative analysis between classical; hybrid; and pure PQC configurations. Designed for academic research and enterprise pre-deployment evaluation. [Note: release date predates FIPS 203/204/205 finalization (Aug 2024); may reference draft/pre-standard algorithms.]

components.name: Q-CORE Q-Scanner
components.description: Free open-source TLS vulnerability auditing tool that analyzes cipher suites, certificates, and quantum readiness across domains. Part of Q-CORE platform with 90+ security modules including Q-AUTOPILOT autonomous SOC orchestrator and Q-CRA EU Cyber Resilience Act compliance dashboard. Supports broad PQC algorithm portfolio across tiered offerings.

components.name: PQCryptoLib-Core

OpenSSL integration via provider. CMVP certificate #4800 is Level 1 (not Level 3), validated 2024-09-16 for PQCryptoLib v1.0.0 covering classical algorithms only (no PQC in validated scope). ACVP certs: A3011 (v1.0.0), A7693 (v1.0.2), A6553 (v3.0.0). PQC-inclusive CMVP module (with ML-KEM/ML-DSA) on the NIST Modules-in-Process/IUT list. Targets enterprise and government deployments.

components.name: Crucible

ML-DSA: 51 tests across 6 categories (norm checks; arithmetic operations; signing determinism; verification robustness; serialization; timing consistency). Uses a language-agnostic JSON line protocol enabling harness support for C; C++; Go; Java; Rust; and other languages. Ships with harnesses for 15 production implementations including CIRCL; liboqs; AWS-LC; Go stdlib; and Bouncy Castle. Created by Symbolic Software.

components.name: Cisco Catalyst Center

components.name: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS

Migration path: use OpenBao 2.x with Go 1.24+ for PQC transport; pair with oqs-provider for ML-DSA signing via OpenSSL subprocess. Actively tracked in OpenBao GitHub issues. Integrates with OPA for policy enforcement — checking if detected algorithms are quantum-safe. Sandbox cbom-compliance scenario feeds CBOMkit output to OPA, which evaluates a Rego policy to detect CNSA 2.0 violations and emit structured violation reports. OPA itself has no crypto; it is the policy enforcement layer above crypto discovery tools.

components.name: cdxgen

Sandbox scenarios use cdxgen to scan the running container filesystem (--type os) to produce a real CBOM covering OpenSSL version, softhsmv3, strongSwan, cosign and all installed tools — which OPA then evaluates against a CNSA 2.0 Rego policy.

Verified by execution on 2026-08-09: ML-DSA-65 Create+Sign and ML-KEM-768 Create+Encapsulate+Decapsulate all succeeded against a live server, with 6 managed objects and an audit trail reporting 37 policy decisions, 78 KMIP operations and 14 PKCS#11 calls. components.name: age-plugin-pqkem

Tracked here to document the gap. Note: age v1.3.0 now provides native hybrid ML-KEM-768 recipients, superseding the need for this plugin (see the "age (file encryption)" row).

components.name: mtc (Merkle Tree Certificates CLI)

The installed v0.1.2 implements a pre-PLANTS draft revision (api label v04b), differing from draft-ietf-plants-merkle-tree-certs-04. It cannot parse NIST ML-DSA SPKI OIDs, so assertion subject keys fall back to P-256 (disclosed via subject_key_fallback_reason). No TLS stack negotiates MTC in the sandbox; the scenario covers cert management and size only.

components.name: Rosenpass

It performs an ML-KEM-based handshake and rotates the WireGuard pre-shared key roughly every 2 minutes, giving WireGuard tunnels post-quantum forward secrecy. In the sandbox it replaces the prior fake-PQC WireGuard script (which used SHA-256 of an ML-KEM public key as the PSK). Architectural note: Rosenpass uses its own internal liboqs PQC backend, NOT the pqctoday-hsm PKCS#11 backend — the only sandbox scenario with this exception, disclosed in the scenario JSON.

components.name: strongSwan (pqctoday-hsm PQC fork)
components.description: strongSwan 6.0.7 patched by pqctoday-hsm (strongswan-pqc.patch, strongswan-pqc-supplement.patch, strongswan-pqc-slhdsa.patch, plus a PKCS#11 plugin patch) to add post-quantum IKEv2 AUTHENTICATION on top of upstream's ML-KEM key exchange. The patches introduce KEY_ML_DSA_44/65/87 and SIGN_ML_DSA_44/65/87 to libstrongswan's key-type and signature-scheme enums, the id-ml-dsa-* OIDs, and proposal keywords (mldsa65 / ike:mldsa65); private keys stay in a softhsmv3 PKCS#11 v3.2 token and are never exported. UPSTREAM strongSwan does NOT ship this -- those enum values do not exist in 6.0.7 and its first-party release notes document ML-KEM key exchange only, with IKEv2 authentication remaining PSK/RSA/ECDSA. See the separate `strongswan` row for the upstream product; this row is the fork.

components.name: softhsmrustv3 (pqctoday Rust PKCS#11 engine)
components.description: Pure-Rust PKCS#11 v3.2 engine, the second crypto backend in pqctoday-hsm alongside the C++ softhsmv3. It is the production backend for the pqctoday-kmip server and the CACP policy engine, and it compiles to wasm32-unknown-emscripten as a staticlib linked into openssl.wasm for the in-browser playground. Carries its own checked-in PKCS#11 v3.2 conformance evidence (rust/RUST_P11_V32_CONFORMANCE_REPORT.md). Since 2026-08-08 it also emits a runtime-gated PKCS#11 operation-evidence log, so a caller can prove which mechanism executed inside the token rather than asserting it.

components.name: bench-harness (pqctoday PKCS#11 benchmark)
components.description: Rust benchmark harness in pqctoday-hsm that drives a PKCS#11 v3.2 engine directly and reports per-mechanism throughput across a 26-algorithm matrix (16 signature, 10 key agreement). It is what the sandbox hsm-perf-bench scenario measures. Published ops/sec figures must come from a run with the engine's operation log DISABLED — at roughly 62,000 signs/sec an enabled log measures the logger rather than the HSM.

components.name: age-plugin-pqctoday
components.description: pqctoday's age recipient plugin implementing the X-Wing hybrid KEM (X25519 + ML-KEM-768) so age — and therefore SOPS — can wrap secrets to a post-quantum recipient. The post-quantum key material is generated in and held by softhsmv3 over PKCS#11 rather than in a file. This is the component that gives the sandbox's SOPS GitOps scenario its PQC; SOPS itself has none (see the getsops-sops row).

components.name: OpenSSL 3.6
components.description: OpenSSL 3.6.x carries ML-KEM, ML-DSA and SLH-DSA natively — no external provider — plus the hybrid TLS 1.3 groups (X25519MLKEM768, SecP256r1MLKEM768, SecP384r1MLKEM1024). This is the branch the pqctoday sandbox builds every scenario against. IMPORTANT: 3.6 is NOT an LTS branch and reaches end of life on 2026-11-01; the LTS branch is 3.5.x, supported to 2030-04-08, which carries the same PQC algorithm set. Anyone adopting 3.6 for PQC should plan the move to an LTS or later branch before that date.
